note: Labelled cases for judge-claims.mjs, lifted from docs/citation-claims-review.md. Every entry was decided by a human reading the paper against the sentence, before any model was involved. `ref` is the 1-indexed narrative reference number the register uses; `pmidHint` is asserted at load time so a shifted reference list fails loudly instead of silently grading the wrong paper. The `sound` cases matter more than the `flag` cases: a judge that flags SULFOX[10] trains the reader to skim, which is worse than no judge.

cases.why: Gao 1999 is a cloning and mutational-analysis study. It cannot establish the malonic:methylmalonic ratio cut-off the sentence uses to discriminate MLYCD from MMUT.
de Wit 2006 is a single case report on neuroimaging, carrying four general claims including a prognosis statement about the main determinant of mortality.
Soler-Alfonso 2015 identifies HIBCH mutations. It reports no therapy trial and no dietary outcome, yet carries the valine-restriction efficacy claim.
Arias 2004 measures the right analytes in the wrong population — urea cycle defects, not creatine transporter deficiency. Screening performance does not transfer.
Frater-Schroder 1983 predates routine holo-TC assays and cannot carry a modern diagnostic algorithm.
A glycogen storage disease type III paper. It may have been cited for the ketone-body therapy principle, but that intent is not visible to a reader.
Efron 1965 is familial HYPERprolinaemia (PRODH). Hydroxyprolinaemia is PRODH2 — a different disorder.

Koeberl 2003 supports the existence of an NBS-detected 3-MCC cohort but not the specific '~1:36,000 in the USA' incidence figure the sentence gives. The citation was repaired; the number was never sourced.

A cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate trial in molybdenum cofactor deficiency, which never mentions sulfite oxidase. Correct: the sentence explicitly contrasts SUOX with MoCo type A, which does have a specific treatment.
A biotinidase deficiency review, because the claim is that biotin-responsive 3-MCC usually indicates biotinidase or holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency.
Menkes 1954, the historical first description. It predates the name 'maple syrup urine disease' and so shares no vocabulary with the modern sentence.
Carson and Neill 1962, the survey in which homocystinuria was first detected. Same historical pattern as Menkes.

Kurosawa's cyclocreatine-in-mice study supports 'cyclocreatine and gene therapy in development'. An earlier review flagged this on the strength of the FABRICATED title it used to carry; the repaired citation fits the claim.
